subject: Post-call: pricing & batching assumptions for Acme Robotics POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme-robotics.com>, Sandeep Rao <s.rao@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: pricing & batching assumptions for Acme Robotics POC

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and next steps from our side.

Key assumptions we heard from Acme during the call:
- Expected monthly token volume: ~10M–30M tokens (you mentioned "starting closer to 20M", correct?)
- Avg tokens per interactive request: ~300–800 tokens (you said many sessions include long context + responses)
- Workload split: ~60% interactive (low-latency chat), ~40% async/batch (nightly processing)
- Concurrency: steady-state ~50–150 concurrent active users; short peaks to ~350–450 for 2–3 minute bursts during shift changes
- Target budget: $5k–$15k / month; target unit economics: ~$350–400 per 1M tokens (goal to keep total cost predictable)

Implications for batching and concurrency (first-pass):
- Continuous batching (long-lived connections + overlapping token generation) will substantially improve unit cost vs per-request dispatch. For mixed interactive+batch patterns we typically see an effective batch size in the 32–64 range depending on request overlap and latencies.
- For interactive traffic (low-latency), we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for system & persona prompts to reduce compute per token.
- For your peak concurrency, plan for additional serving capacity to keep p95 latency targets under 300ms for interactive flows.

Attachments: I attached a light pricing model and a draft POC mutual action plan (POC-MAP.docx) so you can see the line items we typically include.

Next steps / asks from Acme to firm up a quote and POC:
1) Confirm monthly token target (your best estimate for month 1 and month 6).
2) Send a small usage histogram (tokens/request distribution, times-of-day) and a few representative payloads (system + user prompts).
3) Confirm procurement timeline and any required NDAs/PO templates.

If that looks right I'll loop in Aditya (solutions eng) to scope the POC performance targets and get a firm price / recommended quantization profile.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx, POC-MAP.docx

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme-robotics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: pricing & batching assumptions for Acme Robotics POC

Thanks Marissa — nice summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volume: we're expecting ~20M tokens/month in month 1, with a target of 50–60M by month 6 if POC goes well.
2) Avg tokens/request: closer to ~800 tokens on average (we have fairly long context windows for the robotic diagnostics).
3) Traffic split: sounds right — interactive latency-sensitive ops (~60%) and heavier nightly batch jobs (~40%).
4) Budget: procurement is comfortable with ~$10k/month initially. Our internal target for cost/efficiency would be in the $350–400 / 1M tokens range.

Question for Redwood: with our traffic shape (longer sequences + mixed async) what continuous batching improvement should we expect? Specifically, can you validate whether you can hit an effective $/1M token of ~$350 with the batching + quantization steps you suggested? Also, what latency hit do we see for interactive requests when using batching on your platform? Our p95 target for interactive is <= 300ms.

Procurement/Legal: we'll need a standard PO and basic SOC2 evidence. We can share templates next week.

Happy to jump on a short follow-up if helpful.

—Jordan
Head of AI Platform, Acme Robotics
j.ellis@acme-robotics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: pricing & batching assumptions for Acme Robotics POC

Looping you both in — Jordan confirmed ~20M tokens/month (ramp to 50–60M by month 6), avg ~800 tokens/request, budget ~$10k/mo, target $350–400 / 1M tokens. Key asks: can we provide an estimate that meets $350/1M tokens given batching + quantization? p95 latency requirement <= 300ms for interactive.

Notes / proposed approach:
- Continuous batching: for mixed interactive + batch workloads we typically expect 2x–3x effective cost reduction relative to naive per-request processing. That assumes long-lived connections, small per-request arrival jitter (so batches form), and enabling prefix caching. With Acme's 800-token avg, the savings are meaningful because a larger fraction of compute is per-token generation (so batching helps).
- Effective batch size: estimate 32–64 on steady traffic; during peaks we can get 96+ for short windows. Recommend targeting an effective batch size of 48 in the quote.
- Concurrency mapping: rough mapping = steady-state concurrency 150 => ~N nodes (I'll leave capacity calc to Aditya), peak bursts to 400 will need ~3–4x capacity for short windows to keep p95 under 300ms.
- Quantization profile: INT8 or OPTQ options can reduce cost further; we'll propose a conservative fp16->int8 profile for POC and measure regen quality on sample prompts.

Aditya: can you validate expected $/1M with the above assumptions (20M/mo, eff batch size 48, avg 800 tokens, quant profile INT8 conservative) and produce a line-item quote for the POC? Please include any caveats on latency vs batching.

Rachel: can you pull the SOC2/Procurement artifacts and confirm the procurement path (PO template + NDA).

I'll prepare an updated POC MAP and share a proposed timeline (30-day POC, 1-week ramp) once we have the cost table.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme-robotics.com>, Sandeep Rao <s.rao@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: pricing & batching assumptions for Acme Robotics POC

Jordan — thanks for the quick clarifications and the budget guidance. Attaching a short mutual action plan (POC-MAP.docx) and a first-pass pricing workbook (redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx).

Proposed next steps:
1) POC scope: 30-day POC with 1-week ramp (validation on representative workloads + latency targets).
2) Success criteria: ingest 20M tokens over the POC period, p95 interactive latency <= 300ms, measured quality/regression thresholds on sample eval set.
3) Technical onboarding: schedule a 60-minute kickoff with Aditya (Solutions Eng) and your infra lead next week to collect payload samples and confirm traffic shaping. Suggested slots: Wed/Thu morning PST.
4) Procurement: please send your PO template and SOC2 contact; Rachel will follow up with the compliance pack.

We can structure the POC pricing to aim for ~$350 / 1M tokens effective based on continuous batching + INT8 quantization. Caveats: this is an estimate — final unit economics will depend on how the traffic overlaps and how often prefix caching reduces model work. We will instrument the POC and provide weekly token-cost reports so we can iterate on batching configs.

Can you share a 24-hour usage histogram and 3 representative request payloads (system + user message) before EOD Wednesday? That will let us lock an accurate quote and the quant profile to run during POC.

Onboarding call: Aditya — can you propose 2 slots Wed/Thu morning PST?

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
